% A LaTeX document as a PERSON writes one, which is not how pandoc writes one.
%
% pandoc wraps every heading in \hypertarget{id}{%\n\section{...}\label{id}} -- the
% \section sits two braces deep, behind a comment token. A human writes \section at the
% top level and never emits \hypertarget at all. That is the same shape as the RTF and
% DOCX heading split, except the second "writer" here is a person rather than a program.
%
% This comment must not appear in any block.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\usepackage{ulem}
\title{Handwritten}
\author{Nobody}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Heading One}
\label{sec:one}

A paragraph with \textbf{bold}, \emph{italic}, and \sout{strike} text.

\subsection{Heading Two}

\begin{itemize}
  \item bullet one
  \item bullet two
\end{itemize}

\begin{quote}
A block quote.
\end{quote}

Unicode: café --- em-dash, and a tab.

\end{document}
